01Arrival

We built this house around a simple belief: a mountain is not a view. It is a way of spending a day.

PSM Resort sits on the shoulder of a quiet valley, an hour from the nearest town and further still from the nearest hurry. The house is deliberately small. Fourteen rooms, a stove room, a bath, and one long table where everyone eats together.

Come for the snow or come for the heat. The house keeps its own time either way — shaped by light, weather, and whatever the garden decides to give us.

02Rooms

Three ways to stay. None of them try too hard.

The Larch Room

A quiet corner room lined in untreated larch. A deep window seat, a stove that takes the edge off the morning, and a view that changes colour every hour.

28 m²Valley side · first lightEnquire about this room →

The Morning Room

Our most requested room. Tall shutters open onto the terrace, where coffee arrives before anyone else is awake. Linen, stone, and very little else.

34 m²South terrace · full day sunEnquire about this room →

The Ridge Suite

Two rooms under one roof with a private sitting stove and a bath set against the glass. Made for long evenings when the valley has gone dark.

52 m²West ridge · evening lightEnquire about this room →
Pl. 05 — The long table
03Table

Dinner is at seven. You come when you are hungry.

There is no à la carte and there are no two identical evenings. The kitchen sends what arrived that morning to one long oak table. Wine is local, pours are generous, and nobody leaves hungry.

A typical evening — illustrative menu

To beginCeleriac, smoked butter, mountain herbs
From the valleyChar, fermented cabbage, brown butter
From the gardenBeetroot, sheep's yoghurt, dill oil
To finishQuince, honey, sour cream
04Bath

Water, stone, and the deliberate absence of everything else.

The bathhouse is the quietest room in the house. A wood-fired pool, a cold plunge cut into the stone, and a resting room with windows facing the ridge. Phones stay in the bedrooms. So do your plans.

  • 06:30 Cold plunge, if you dare
  • 11:00 Wood-fired pool, steam room
  • 17:00 Quiet hour — no talking
✳
05Field notes

Things worth getting up for.

The long way up

On foot · 3 hours

Leave before the light reaches the ridge. The trail passes two abandoned sawmills and arrives at a bench we did not build but have come to consider ours.

Cold water, warm stone

Every morning · 07:00

A short walk through the snow to the wood-fired pool. There is no programme, no music, and no reason to stay longer than you want to.

One table, one evening

Thursday · 19:30

Guests and cooks eat together at the long oak table. What is served depends on what came down the valley that morning.
